newsitem.title: DENMARK: GN Store Nord sees Sonofon profit in 1997.
newsitem.headline: GN Store Nord sees Sonofon profit in 1997.

text.p: Danish cable and telecoms group GN Store Nord posted on Tuesday 16 per cent higher pre-tax profits and said it expected its partly-owned mobile telephone unit Sonofon to swing into profit for the first time in 1997.

"The group's plan to become a significant telecoms operator in Denmark is expected to be realised with Sonofon...1997 is to be the first year in which Sonofon makes a positive contribution to overall group operating profits," GN Store Nord said in a statement accompanying its 1996 results.

It said Sonofon almost doubled its mobile telephone subscribers to 510,000 in 1996 and that this accounted for much of the 27 percent increase in overall group turnover to 2.722 billion crowns ($421.5 million).
GN Store Nord said that telecommunications and industrial activities accounted each for about half of total group turnover in 1996 at 1.3 billion and 1.4 billion crowns respectively.
GN Store Nord's 53.5 percent-owned Sonofon competes with maket-leader Tele Danmark in the mobile telephones market in Denmark as the industry undergoes deregulation.
U.S. Bell-South holds the remaining 46.5 percent stake in Sonofon.

GN Store Nord posted 1996 profit before tax and extraordinary items of 213 million crowns, 15.7 percent up on 1995, more or less in line with analysts' expectations and forecast a better result in 1997, without naming any figure.

It said it estimated that Sonofon had a negative effect of 29 million crowns, due to major promotional costs in competing with Tele Danmark in a cut-throat domestic market but said that nonetheless Sonofon did better than before.

It said it planned to expand Sonofon activities further in 1997, offering new products and services using existing and new technologies and introducing international long distance (ILD) tariffs for customers on both mobile and fixed networks.

Otherwise the group's Great Nordic Telegraph Company unit suffered falling earnings from its Denmark-Russia telecommunications cable but it said negotiations were afoot on new international cable projects in Europe and the Far East.
The market took the GN Store Nord result largely in its stride and the share traded five crowns down at 690 at 1125 gmt. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652 ($ = 6.458 Danish Crowns)
